links.reading: William, your steady attention can help Charlotte feel safe sharing what she likes. Charlotte, you may find it easier to show affection through small choices, such as asking him to join a game. William, let her choose how much to share, and do not press when she wants privacy. Behaviour check: Notice whether Charlotte volunteers something she enjoyed this week.

William, your practical help can give Charlotte confidence to keep trying at homework. Charlotte, you may bring persistence and energy to a task you care about. This works best when William offers help without taking over. Too much help can make her feel the answer is no longer hers. Behaviour check: At the kitchen table, let Charlotte try before you step in.

William, you may hold firmly to a household rule when Charlotte pushes for change. Charlotte, you may keep testing that rule when it feels unfair. This can make a small disagreement last longer than either of you wants. You can use it to practise explaining the reason and hearing her view. Behaviour check: Name the rule plainly and ask Charlotte what feels unfair.

William, you may think an instruction was clear while Charlotte is still working out what you mean. Charlotte, you may hesitate to say you heard something different. During the morning rush, that gap can turn a simple request into frustration. A short check gives her time to answer and correct you. Behaviour check: Ask Charlotte what she heard before repeating the instruction.

William, you may assume a kind offer is what Charlotte wants, while she may hope you notice a different need. Charlotte, you can help by saying whether you want company, help, or time alone. Guessing can leave both of you disappointed. Clear choices make care easier to receive. Behaviour check: Ask Charlotte what kind of help she wants with one task.

William, a quick change in plans may make you give a new instruction before Charlotte is ready to respond. Charlotte, you may need a moment to gather your thoughts, then explain what you understood. That pause can look like refusal when it is not. Waiting briefly helps her practise answering clearly. Behaviour check: Give Charlotte a moment to answer during the morning rush.

William, you can offer a dependable time for the Sunday call. Charlotte, you may have ideas about whom to include or what to share. A plan can hold both your need for follow-through and her wish to contribute. Make the details clear, then leave room for her suggestions. Behaviour check: Agree together on the call time and who will join.

William, you may want a familiar routine to stay in place. Charlotte, you may ask to change it when your interests shift. If the answer is simply no, she may stop explaining; if plans keep changing, you may lose trust in them. A clear boundary with a fair choice helps both. Behaviour check: Set a tablet stopping point and hear Charlotte's request.

William, you may notice when Charlotte is upset even if she has not explained why. Charlotte, you may feel his attention strongly and want to choose when to talk. Staying nearby without asking repeated questions lets her decide. Your closeness can support trust, but pressing for an answer may make her withdraw. Behaviour check: After a game loss, offer company and let Charlotte choose whether to talk.

William, you may want a routine that works and lasts. Charlotte, you may need to question it or suggest another way. Together, you can make changes without losing the useful parts, though sudden changes may unsettle William. Give Charlotte a say while keeping expectations clear. Behaviour check: Choose one small routine to review together this week.

Charlotte, your everyday needs can draw William into practical tasks, from getting ready to keeping plans on track. William, you may naturally notice what needs doing and step in. That care can help, but she also needs chances to manage age-appropriate tasks herself. Behaviour check: Let Charlotte choose one morning task to handle on her own.

William, Charlotte can bring you into her hopes, friendships, and small joys. Charlotte, you may enjoy sharing a story about school or inviting him into something you care about. Listen without turning every detail into advice. That helps her feel heard while she decides what matters. Behaviour check: Ask Charlotte what she most wants to tell you this week.

William, Charlotte's presence can make your own habits and reactions easier to notice. Charlotte, your questions and choices may shape how he approaches the day. Keep your guidance clear without expecting her to follow your lead in every detail. She is still discovering what suits her. Behaviour check: Ask Charlotte what she wants to try before offering your plan.
